Written by hand.
A module with several packages that each generate part of their own API. The
zip carries the directives and the generator, and not the files the generator
writes. The generator for package broken writes its file and then fails.

-- .mod --
module example.com/generatedpkgs

//go:gendep

go 1.16
-- .info --
{"Version": "v1.0.0"}
-- go.mod --
module example.com/generatedpkgs

//go:gendep

go 1.16
-- gen/main.go --
package main

import (
	"flag"
	"fmt"
	"os"
)

func main() {
	pkg := flag.String("pkg", "", "package the file belongs to")
	out := flag.String("out", "", "file to write")
	fail := flag.Bool("fail", false, "fail after writing the file")
	flag.Parse()
	body := fmt.Sprintf("package %s\n\nfunc Name() string { return %q }\n", *pkg, *pkg)
	if err := os.WriteFile(*out, []byte(body), 0o666); err != nil {
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	if *fail {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "broken on purpose")
		os.Exit(1)
	}
}
-- one/one.go --
//go:generate go run example.com/generatedpkgs/gen -pkg one -out one.gen.go

// Package one declares nothing itself: Name is the generator's to write.
package one
-- two/two.go --
//go:generate go run example.com/generatedpkgs/gen -pkg two -out two.gen.go

// Package two declares nothing itself: Name is the generator's to write.
package two
-- three/three.go --
//go:generate go run example.com/generatedpkgs/gen -pkg three -out three.gen.go

// Package three declares nothing itself: Name is the generator's to write.
package three
-- broken/broken.go --
//go:generate go run example.com/generatedpkgs/gen -pkg broken -out broken.gen.go -fail

// Package broken declares nothing itself, and its generator fails.
package broken
